title: `ObjectGrid`'s inline add-record row rides on the author-declared `operations.create` with no `can(object,'create')` gate
body:
## Summary

Found while implementing #5143 (gating `ObjectGrid`'s `editable` key on `can(object, 'update')`). Filed rather than fixed, per the scope rule — it is the `create` face of the same shape and was outside that PR's radius.

## Evidence (`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, on `dfc697554`)

The Airtable-style inline "add record" row is gated on the author-declared operation alone:

```ts
// line ~2782
showAddRow: !!operations?.create,
onAddRecord: onAddRecord,
```

`operations` is `schema.operations` when declared, otherwise the `{ update: !!onEdit, delete: !!onDelete }` default — an authoring flag that says whether the affordance was *wired*, never a permission grant. Grepping the whole component for the principal's create verdict returns nothing:

```
$ grep -n "can(objectName, 'create')" packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx
(no matches — the only hit for 'create' is a comment on line 724)
```

Contrast the two neighbours resolved a few lines apart at ~730, both of which ARE consumed: `permissionUpdate` / `permissionDelete` feed `resolveRowCrudAffordances`, and after #5143 `permissionUpdate` also feeds the inline-edit verdict. There is no `permissionCreate` at all.

## Consequence, stated honestly

Same round-trip shape as #5143 and #4646: a principal with no `create` grant is offered the add-row, fills it in, and is stopped only by the server's 403. No data lands — the server gate is solid — but the UI walks the user through a write it knows will fail, while the toolbar's New button on the very same screen hides itself for that principal.

**Reachability today is the reason this is filed as an observation rather than a live defect, and the reason the label is `finding`:** nothing shipped declares `operations: { create: true }` on an `object-grid`. Grepping `packages/`, `apps/` and `examples/` finds the key only in three tests, and all three set it to `false`. So the affordance is dormant unless an author writes the key — which is a real, declared authoring surface, and exactly the audience #5143 was about. Triage may well grade this higher than I have; the severity call is deliberately left to the triage round rather than guessed at filing time.

## Suggested shape

The conjunction the sibling gates already use, with the operation moved to `create`:

```ts
const permissionCreate = objectName ? perms.can(objectName, 'create') : undefined;
// then: showAddRow: !!operations?.create && (permissionCreate ?? true)
```

`can()` answers `true` with no `PermissionProvider`, so standalone embeds and the Studio designer keep today's behaviour — the fail-open every sibling gate in this file relies on. Whether the object's resolved `create` affordance (ADR-0103 bucket ∧ `userActions.create` ∧ the server's effective API operations) should join it, the way #5143 folded `isObjectInlineEditable` into the update verdict, is the design question worth settling before implementing — `resolveCrudAffordances` already produces `createPredicates` (consumed by the related-list toolbar since #4646 / PR #5145), so there is a resolved answer available to AND with.

## Related (same family — "one affordance missing the gate its siblings have")

- #5143 — the `editable` / inline-edit half of this very component.
- #4646 / #4647 — the related-list "+ New" predicates and the ListView inline-edit toggle (PR #5145).
- #4096 / PR #4108 — row kebab gated on `apiOperations` instead of the caller's permission.
- #4296 — row kebab vs the record-level verdict.
- #3492 — bulk action buttons ignoring `requiredPermissions`.
